title: Citi opens upside catalyst watches on BMW and Forvia

Citi opens upside catalyst watches on BMW and Forvia
Sam Boughedda
Fri, August 28, 2026 at 5:22 AM MDT 1 min read
BMW.DE
C
FRVIA.PA
BMWG
Trade C on Coinbase

Investing.com -- Citi has opened positive catalyst watches on BMW (ETR: BMWG) and Forvia (EPA: FRVIA), arguing that depressed sentiment across European autos has left both names with attractive tactical setups.

On BMW, the bank opened a 90-day upside watch running into the carmaker's Sept. 30 capital markets day, its first under a new chief executive.

Analyst Harald Hendrikse pointed to shares down 38% year to date and trading around 10 euros below net cash, with expectations at record lows. "Will investors further short the shares into the CMD? We don't think so. Rather we believe any positive headlines could in fact lead to some short covering," he wrote.

Citi noted BMW's June profit warning cut full-year auto EBIT margin guidance by 60% to 3% to 5%, the weakest in roughly two decades.

But the bank argued the negative China earnings delta has likely peaked after three consecutive years of warnings, and that shares recovered at least 10 euros within three months of the previous two China warnings.

The bank sees scope for positive surprise through model and technology cuts, lower capex and R&D, and higher cash returns from a record industrial cash balance. BMW remains rated Neutral.

For Forvia, Citi opened a 30-day upside watch ahead of possible European Commission local-content or industry-support measures.

Analyst Ross MacDonald said the shares trade near year-to-date lows despite reaffirmed guidance, with the debate expected to shift toward capital returns in 2027.

Key Points

Interested in JPMorgan Chase & Co.? Here are five stocks we like better.

Situational Awareness reportedly lost 67% in July after leveraged AI stock bets reversed, forcing a broad unwind of public equity holdings.

Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America and Citigroup are reportedly facing SEC subpoenas tied to the fund's trading and lender relationships.

The bank-solvency risk appears limited for now, but investors should watch whether prime brokers tighten margin terms and reduce market liquidity.

When a high-flying fund crashes, the shockwaves can spill beyond its own balance sheet. Following a sharp mid-summer sell-off in the semiconductor sector, the artificial intelligence-focused hedge fund Situational Awareness sustained a devastating 67% portfolio drawdown. To meet escalating margin calls, the fund liquidated the bulk of its public equities at a steep discount. Now, regulators are asking hard questions about the institutions that bankrolled those trades.

The Securities and Exchange Commission recently issued subpoenas to four major Wall Street prime brokers. Regulators want to understand the timing of the fund's trades, its communications with lenders, and how these banks monitored such aggressive leverage. While a regulatory inquiry of this magnitude might sound the alarm for a systemic banking sector crisis, a closer look at the underlying fundamentals tells a different story. The immediate threat does not lie in bank insolvency. The more relevant risk investors need to watch for is the potential for a forced, market-wide deleveraging cycle.

Fortress Balance Sheets: Banks Shrug off the Blow

To understand how the market is digesting this regulatory probe, it helps to look at the financial health of the prime brokers involved. The fundamental baseline for these institutions is incredibly strong, creating a meaningful buffer against immediate liquidity stress.

During the most recent quarter, The Goldman Sachs Group (NYSE: GS) delivered a substantial earnings beat. Goldman Sachs topped consensus earnings per share estimates by over $6.50, while revenue rose nearly 40% year-over-year. Similarly, JPMorgan Chase & Co. (NYSE: JPM) beat consensus estimates by approximately 55 cents per share, backed by a revenue jump of around 27%. These are not institutions showing signs of immediate balance-sheet distress; they are generating billions in operating cash flow.

title: Should You Buy BAC Stock as AI-Led Branch Expansion Boosts Efficiency?
detail:
Should You Buy BAC Stock as AI-Led Branch Expansion Boosts Efficiency?
Nikita Kataruka
Thu, August 27, 2026 at 8:06 AM MDT 8 min read
BAC
C-PR
JPM
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Bank of America BAC has increasingly been using artificial intelligence (AI), digital adoption and branch optimization to improve operating leverage. With more than 69 million consumer and small-business clients, nearly 50 million active digital users, and 3,500 financial centers, BAC has the scale to shift routine servicing to lower-cost digital channels while using branches for higher-value advisory and relationship banking.

AI is central to this strategy. Erica, BAC's AI-powered virtual assistant, has surpassed 3.2 billion client interactions, while generative AI-enabled EricaAssist supports more than 18,000 customer-service representatives. Greater automation across servicing and internal processes could reduce manual workloads, improve productivity and support stronger pretax margins.

Recent results already point to better operating leverage. In the second quarter of 2026, the company's revenues rose 15% year over year to $31.6 billion, while non-interest expenses increased 8% to $18.6 billion. The efficiency ratio improved to 59.02% from 62.61%, net income climbed 27% and the return on average tangible common equity increased to 17.03% from 13.61%.

BAC is complementing its digital push with targeted branch expansion. It plans to open more than 150 financial centers across 60 markets by the end of 2027, while optimizing its existing footprint. This "phygital" strategy could support deposit growth, deepen client relationships and expand cross-selling opportunities without significantly increasing fixed costs. Its proposed investment of up to 49.9% in Jio Credit also provides exposure to India's growing digital lending market.

Thus, investors may be tempted to buy the BAC stock to capitalize on improving operating leverage, AI-led productivity gains and branch optimization. However, the sustainability of these benefits will depend on BAC's ability to convert technology investments into durable expense efficiencies, revenue growth and healthy returns on capital. Therefore, investors should assess the bank's fundamentals and growth outlook before determining whether the stock offers meaningful upside.

Bank of America's Key Fundamental Strengths

Robust Top-Line Growth: Bank of America has maintained a solid revenue growth trajectory over the past several years, supported by expanding loan balances, higher net interest income (NII) and steady growth in fee-based revenues.

The company's net loans and leases saw a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 5.2% from 2020 to 2025. Aided by this loan growth and favorable balance-sheet positioning, NII witnessed a 6.7% CAGR over the same period despite declines in interest rates in 2024 and 2025.

Meanwhile, non-interest income saw a CAGR of 4.7%, helping total revenues see a 5.7% CAGR. The upward momentum in revenues continued in the first half of 2026.

title: Citi sees an opportunity in Oracle after ’one of the most extreme’ stock drawdowns
detail:
Citi sees an opportunity in Oracle after ’one of the most extreme’ stock drawdowns
Sam Boughedda
Wed, August 26, 2026 at 6:44 AM MDT 1 min read
C
ORCL
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Investing.com -- Citi opened a positive catalyst watch on Oracle (NYSE: ORCL) on Wednesday, telling investors that the software group's recent collapse has created an entry point ahead of results and its investor day in late October.

The bank said it sees "opportunity after one of the most extreme dislocations and drawdowns in the stock's history," driven by investor capitulation and technical selling factors including credit spreads and at-the-market equity issuance.

Shares have underperformed nearly all large-cap technology peers by a wide margin over the past three months, with a peak-to-trough drawdown of more than 50% inside 30 to 40 days, a move Citi described as four to five standard deviations against historical volatility.

The bank believes expectations have now reset, with forced selling likely behind the stock and bond and credit default swap spreads recovering.

Furthermore, Citi pointed to strong second-quarter updates from neocloud providers as a positive read-across, saying insatiable demand is driving pricing and margin upside and that Oracle should see similar benefits on newly signed contracts.

It noted Oracle added more than $85 billion of sequential backlog in the May quarter, far above the roughly $9 billion from the neoclouds.

The bank raised its fiscal 2028 to 2030 revenue and earnings estimates, taking its fiscal 2030 EPS forecast to $22, above both Oracle's own $21 target and consensus near $20. Its price target remains $330.
